name: Single-disc Floor Machine
definition: A corded or battery-powered commercial floor-treatment machine that rotates one brush or pad beneath a manually guided head for scrubbing, stripping, spray cleaning, polishing or other manufacturer-approved tasks.
includedScope: Commercial low- and standard-speed single-disc machines
Model-approved brushes, pad drivers, solution tanks and dust-control accessories
excludedScope: Floor sanding, hazardous-area or stone-treatment work unless the exact machine and tooling are approved
headline: Single-disc floor machine types, speed, tooling and buyer verification
description: This technical profile separates machine speed from task suitability and shows buyers how to verify pad diameter, driver, brush, power, chemical and floor compatibility for the exact model.
metaDescription: Commercial single-disc floor machine guide covering rotary types, speed, tooling, specifications, applications and procurement checks.
disclaimer: This is an independent category reference, not model-specific operating, chemical, floor-care or safety advice. Confirm the current manual, machine configuration, floor-finish instructions, tooling part numbers and local electrical requirements before procurement or use.

keyFacts.label: Rotary action
keyFacts.value: One driven disc carries a model-approved brush or pad driver
keyFacts.evidence: Reviewed product pages and manuals describe a single rotating work head and named accessories.
keyFacts.scope: Reviewed commercial single-disc models; no cross-model tooling fit is implied.

keyFacts.label: Reviewed speed range
keyFacts.value: 140–180 rpm for the selected low-speed representative models
keyFacts.evidence: Official model data states 140, 150, 165 or 180 rpm for the named machines.
keyFacts.scope: Selected models only, not a formal boundary for every single-disc machine.

keyFacts.label: Tooling boundary
keyFacts.value: Pad diameter alone does not establish fit or task approval
keyFacts.evidence: Manufacturer documentation identifies model-specific pad holders, brushes and optional accessories.
keyFacts.scope: Exact model, driver interface, diameter, speed rating and regional part number.

systemFlow.name: Power and control
systemFlow.role: Supplies controlled rotation while the operator guides the machine.
systemFlow.evidence: Official manuals describe electrical connection, controls and operating sequence.
systemFlow.scope: Named corded machines; voltage and protection vary by market.

systemFlow.name: Drive transmission
systemFlow.role: Transfers motor output to the fitted driver or brush at the specified speed.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturer specifications publish motor input and rotational speed for named models.
systemFlow.scope: Exact model; published input power is not output at the floor.

systemFlow.name: Floor contact
systemFlow.role: Provides the mechanical action selected for the approved task and floor system.
systemFlow.evidence: Official documentation lists distinct drivers, pads and brushes by application.
systemFlow.scope: Only accessories approved for the exact model and speed.

systemFlow.name: Optional treatment delivery
systemFlow.componentFamily: Solution tank, spray or vacuum accessory
systemFlow.role: Adds controlled liquid delivery or dust collection where the configuration supports it.
systemFlow.evidence: Official ranges list optional tanks or accessory systems for named machines.
systemFlow.scope: Optional equipment; not every model includes recovery or dust collection.

variants.name: Low-speed scrubbing and stripping machine
variants.taskScale: Periodic restorative work and controlled scrubbing
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator guides lateral movement through handle position
variants.spaceConstraints: Requires swing clearance, cord management and stable footing
variants.limitations: Finish removal and floor suitability depend on pad, chemical and coating instructions.
variants.evidence: Official sources position the named low-speed models for scrubbing, stripping or shampooing with approved accessories.

variants.name: Standard-speed multipurpose machine
variants.taskScale: Routine spray cleaning, polishing and light scrubbing
variants.operatorRelationship: Manual guidance with balanced rotary head
variants.spaceConstraints: Turning space and cable route remain critical
variants.limitations: A multipurpose label does not make every pad, chemical or floor compatible.
variants.evidence: Cleanfix and Truvox publish 180 or 200-class multipurpose machines with task-specific accessories.
variants.scope: Reviewed product descriptions; exact instructions govern use.

variants.name: Solution-tank or accessory-equipped configuration
variants.taskScale: Tasks requiring controlled chemical or water delivery
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator controls both machine and liquid application
variants.spaceConstraints: Added tank changes mass, balance and storage envelope
variants.limitations: This is not a scrubber-dryer and normally does not recover solution.
variants.evidence: Manufacturer accessory documentation shows optional solution systems on named ranges.
variants.scope: Quoted accessories and regional configurations only.

performanceMetrics.name: Working width and driver diameter
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Nominal contact width and first filter for tooling selection
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Brush and pad dimensions may be reported differently
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not assume equal nominal diameter means equal hub, center-lock or skirt fit.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official sources publish 400–450 mm class working dimensions for named models.

performanceMetrics.name: Rotational speed
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: One input to the approved task, pad and finish combination
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: No-load or nominal rpm; load and floor conditions differ
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Higher rpm is not automatically better and does not replace task approval.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Manufacturers publish model-specific rpm and application positioning.

performanceMetrics.name: Machine mass and contact pressure
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Affects handling and floor contact when considered with head geometry
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Machine mass, accessory mass and published pressure use different boundaries
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Mass alone does not establish cleaning result or operator effort.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official data publishes weights and, for selected models, brush pressure.

performanceMetrics.name: Input power, voltage and cord
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Supports circuit, plug, extension and route planning
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Regional voltage and cord packages differ
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Input watts do not directly measure floor-treatment performance.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official specifications list nominal power, voltage and cord length for named models.

applicationFit.evidence: Manufacturers list stripping or scrubbing among approved uses for selected low-speed models.
applicationFit.scope: Compatible resilient or hard floors, finishes, chemicals and tooling only.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: The approval chain must include floor manufacturer, finish, chemical, pad and machine.
applicationFit.assessment: Use a small controlled trial and define the required finish-removal or soil-removal result.
applicationFit.basis: Official task positioning plus model-specific accessory systems.
applicationFit.limitations: WCB has not tested coating removal or floor damage.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Submit the exact floor and finish system to the supplier and document the trial settings.

applicationFit.evidence: Reviewed manufacturers position named machines for spray cleaning or polishing.
applicationFit.scope: Manufacturer-approved pad, chemical and floor combinations.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Desired gloss and productivity should be measured on the facility's actual finish.
applicationFit.assessment: Separate routine maintenance from ultra-high-speed burnishing requirements.
applicationFit.basis: Official application labels and published rpm.
applicationFit.limitations: No cross-brand gloss ranking is established.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Trial the exact maintenance chemical and record passes, pad consumption and appearance.

applicationFit.evidence: Selected official ranges list carpet shampooing with named brushes or tanks.
applicationFit.scope: Only models, accessories and carpet systems expressly approved by the manufacturer.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Moisture control and extraction are separate requirements because a single-disc machine does not inherently recover solution.
applicationFit.assessment: Assess pile distortion, wetting, drying and follow-on extraction as one process.
applicationFit.basis: Manufacturer application statements and machine architecture.
applicationFit.limitations: This profile does not establish carpet warranty compatibility.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Obtain written carpet-system approval and specify the recovery and drying method.

componentStack.name: Pad driver or brush interface
componentStack.role: Connects the working tool to the machine drive.
componentStack.evidence: Manufacturer sources list model-specific drivers and brushes.
componentStack.scope: Family labels do not establish cross-model compatibility.

componentStack.name: Pad or abrasive system
componentStack.role: Provides the selected level of cleaning, stripping or polishing action.
componentStack.evidence: Official accessory systems differentiate pads by task.
componentStack.scope: Color naming is not assumed equivalent across suppliers.

componentStack.name: Power and cord set
componentStack.role: Supplies the motor and safety controls.
componentStack.evidence: Official specifications show regional electrical values and cord lengths.

componentStack.name: Optional solution or dust accessory
componentStack.role: Supports liquid delivery or dust management for approved tasks.
variants: Vacuum or dust skirt on selected models
componentStack.evidence: Manufacturers list optional accessories by product family.
componentStack.scope: Accessory presence and compatibility must be confirmed by part number.

Nilfisk publishes the model identity and cited configuration data.

representativeModels.marketScope: TASKI global product page and information sheet
representativeModels.evidence: TASKI publishes the cited technical data and task positioning.
representativeModels.scope: Reviewed global documentation; confirm local type.

representativeModels.evidence: Cleanfix publishes the cited values for R 44-180.

representativeModels.marketScope: Columbus international product page and data sheet
representativeModels.evidence: Columbus publishes the cited technical data.
representativeModels.scope: Named model; regional accessories require confirmation.

representativeModels.marketScope: Numatic UK page and official data sheet
representativeModels.evidence: Numatic publishes the cited specifications for HFM1515-R.
Truvox identifies the model and its multipurpose positioning and accessories.
representativeModels.scope: Official product page; confirm current regional specification.

procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Selecting by rpm or pad color alone
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official documentation separates applications and model-specific accessories.
procurementDecisions.scope: Exact floor system and named machine.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Procurement should treat the treatment system as one verified configuration.
procurementDecisions.basis: Manufacturers publish tasks and tooling within model boundaries.
procurementDecisions.limitations: No universal pad-color or chemical equivalence is established.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Require a written configuration schedule and representative floor trial.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Record machine product number, driver, pad, chemical dilution and floor-finish approval.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Handling, cord routing and changeover time
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official data documents mass, cord and accessory arrangements.
procurementDecisions.scope: Named corded machines and actual site route.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Achieved output includes transport, cord moves, pad changes and solution handling.
procurementDecisions.limitations: WCB has not timed the routes.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Run a full-route trial including setup and cleanup.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Verify circuit locations, stairs, storage, transport mass and cable protection.

engineeringChecks.reason: Diameter and family names do not prove mechanical fit or speed approval.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Match every driver, brush, pad and optional tank to the exact product and serial range.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official manuals and accessory lists are model-specific.

engineeringChecks.reason: Voltage, plug, protection and cable placement affect safe operation.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Confirm the regional electrical configuration and complete a site cord-routing assessment.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official specifications publish model-specific electrical and cord data.

engineeringChecks.reason: Aggressive tooling or unsuitable chemicals can alter or damage a floor system.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Obtain written floor/finish approval and document a small-area trial.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Manufacturer documentation limits machines to approved tasks and accessories.
engineeringChecks.scope: Exact site floor, finish, pad and chemical.

standards.name: IEC 60335-2-67:2021
standards.applicability: Particular safety requirements for powered floor treatment machines intended for commercial indoor or outdoor use.
standards.evidence: IEC lists the valid fifth edition and the commercial floor-treatment machine scope.
standards.scope: Confirm regional adoption and exact machine classification.

developments.title: IEC commercial floor-treatment safety edition published
developments.summary: IEC published edition 5.0 of IEC 60335-2-67 for powered commercial floor treatment machines.
developments.evidence: The IEC catalogue records the publication date, edition and valid status.
developments.scope: International base standard; regional conformity routes differ.
